reports_summary.excerpt:
INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with painful desmoid for cryoablation (attn.
Dr. ___  // ___ year old woman with painful desmoid for cryoablation (attn.
Dr. ___

EXAMINATION:  CT-guided cryoablation

COMPARISON:  MRI abdomen and pelvis ___

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___, radiology trainee and Dr. ___
___, attending radiologist. Dr. ___ supervised the trainee
during the key components of the procedure and reviewed and agree with the
trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA:  General anesthesia was administered by the anesthesiology
department.
MEDICATIONS:  For full details please refer to anesthesiology notes.
CONTRAST: None
RADIATION DOSE: Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 9.4 s, 27.0 cm; CTDIvol = 19.7 mGy (Body) DLP = 506.7
mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 6.4 s, 19.5 cm; CTDIvol = 22.1 mGy (Body) DLP = 414.4
mGy-cm.
   3) Stationary Acquisition 2.9 s, 1.4 cm; CTDIvol = 30.1 mGy (Body) DLP =
43.4 mGy-cm.
   4) Spiral Acquisition 6.4 s, 19.5 cm; CTDIvol = 20.7 mGy (Body) DLP = 376.7
mGy-cm.
   5) Stationary Acquisition 1.4 s, 1.4 cm; CTDIvol = 15.1 mGy (Body) DLP =
21.7 mGy-cm.
   6) Spiral Acquisition 19.1 s, 19.5 cm; CTDIvol = 57.2 mGy (Body) DLP =
1,042.9 mGy-cm.
   7) Spiral Acquisition 25.5 s, 19.5 cm; CTDIvol = 76.1 mGy (Body) DLP =
1,387.1 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 3,805 mGy-cm.

PROCEDURE:  PROCEDURE DETAILS:

Following explanation of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the
procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient. The patient
was then brought to the computed tomography suite and placed supine on the
imaging table.  General anesthesia was induced by the anesthesiologist. 
Following
scout imaging, the skin was marked and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Under ultrasound and CT fluoroscopy, four 3.8 mm and two 2.4 mm cryoprobes
were placed in a parallel orientation along the long axis of the tumor from a
lateral to medial approach spaced approximately 2 cm apart and extending close
to the medial margin of the tumor.  15 minutes of freezing followed by 10
minutes following and an additional 15 minutes of freezing was performed.  The
cryoprobes were pulled back approximately 5 cm and this more proximal portion
of the tumor was treated in the same fashion.  2 of the probes were turned off
during portions of freezing as freezing was adequately achieved along these
margins.

Post procedural computed tomography demonstrated a large iceball occupying
approximately 70% of the tumor volume.  The skin was then cleaned and a dry
sterile dressing was applied. The patient was awakened from general anesthesia
without incident and there were no immediate post-procedure complications. The
patient was transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit
for further monitoring.

FINDINGS: 

Re- demonstrated is a large mass within the right lower quadrant measuring up
to 14 cm compatible with the patient's known biopsy-proven desmoid tumor.  No
other intra-abdominal or intrapelvic abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION: 

CT-guided cryoablation of a large abdominal desmoid tumor.  It is estimated
that 70% of the tumor volume was ablated.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  The patient is scheduled to return for cryoablation of the
residual tumor in 3 weeks.

    PROCEDURE:  PROCEDURE DETAILS:
    
    Following explanation of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the
    procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient. The patient
    was then brought to the computed tomography suite and placed supine on the
    imaging table.  General anesthesia was induced by the anesthesiologist. 
    Following
    scout imaging, the skin was marked and draped in the usual sterile fashion.
    
    Under ultrasound and CT fluoroscopy, four 3.8 mm and two 2.4 mm cryoprobes
    were placed in a parallel orientation along the long axis of the tumor from a
    lateral to medial approach spaced approximately 2 cm apart and extending close
    to the medial margin of the tumor.  15 minutes of freezing followed by 10
    minutes following and an additional 15 minutes of freezing was performed.  The
    cryoprobes were pulled back approximately 5 cm and this more proximal portion
    of the tumor was treated in the same fashion.  2 of the probes were turned off
    during portions of freezing as freezing was adequately achieved along these
    margins.
    
    Post procedural computed tomography demonstrated a large iceball occupying
    approximately 70% of the tumor volume.  The skin was then cleaned and a dry
    sterile dressing was applied. The patient was awakened from general anesthesia
    without incident and there were no immediate post-procedure complications. The
    patient was transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit
    for further monitoring.
